description: Experience the iconic flavors of India with our authentic Tandoori Chicken, perfectly grilled over charcoal. Marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, the chicken becomes incredibly tender and infused with a smoky char. This classic dish promises a delightful culinary journey, ideal for a memorable Indian dinner.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make deep gashes or slits all over the chicken pieces. This allows the marinades to penetrate deeply, ensuring maximum flavor and tenderness.

instructions.title: First Marinade Application
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub this mixture well into all the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the slits. Let it rest for 15 minutes. This step helps tenderize the chicken and adds a foundational layer of flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, mix the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, remaining 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, 0.5 teaspoon of salt, mustard oil, and optional food color. Whisk everything together until you have a smooth, well-combined paste.

instructions.title: Second Marinade and Marination
instructions.text: Add the chicken from the first marinade to the bowl with the second marinade. Ensure every piece of chicken is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for the best flavor infusion and tenderization.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30-40 minutes before you plan to cook, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the coals for indirect heat, with a hot zone for searing and a cooler zone for slower cooking. The ideal temperature for grilling Tandoori Chicken is medium-high, around 375-400°F (190-200°C).

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals initially for about 2-3 minutes per side to get a nice char. Then move them to the cooler part of the grill to cook through slowly. Baste the chicken frequently with melted butter or oil during cooking. Turn the pieces every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking and prevent burning. Continue grilling for about 25-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) and the chicken is tender and cooked through.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve immediately with lemon wedges, mint chutney, or sliced onions. It pairs wonderfully with naan bread, roti, or a simple rice pilaf.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, ensure your yogurt is thick and drained of excess water. This helps the marinade cling better to the chicken.
Do not skip the deep gashes on the chicken; they are crucial for the marinade to penetrate and for the chicken to cook evenly and remain juicy.
When grilling, control flare-ups by moving chicken to a cooler zone or by spraying with water. Basting regularly keeps the chicken moist and adds flavor.
article:
Craving that iconic, smoky flavor of authentic Indian cuisine? Look no further than Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. This beloved dish, with its vibrant color, tender meat, and charred edges, is a staple in Indian restaurants worldwide, and for good reason. While often associated with the traditional clay tandoor oven, recreating its magic at home on a charcoal grill is not only achievable but incredibly rewarding. Get ready to embark on a culinary journey that will bring the heart of India right to your backyard.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?
Tandoori chicken is a classic Indian dish originating from the Punjab region, famed for its distinct red hue and succulent texture. Traditionally cooked in a cylindrical clay oven known as a tandoor, the high heat and smoky environment impart an unparalleled flavor. When we talk about Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, we're aiming to replicate that authentic experience. The chicken is marinated in a rich mixture of yogurt and a potent blend of spices – including ginger, garlic, red chili, cumin, coriander, and garam masala. The yogurt acts as a tenderizer, while the spices infuse the meat with layers of complex flavor. Grilling it over hot coals not only adds that coveted smoky char but also helps lock in the juices, ensuring every bite is moist and flavorful. This method truly elevates the dish, making it a spectacular centerpiece for any Indian dinner.

## Ingredients You Need
To create this magnificent Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, gather the following:

For the Chicken:
*   1 whole chicken (about 3-4 lbs), cut into 8 pieces, or 8 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice
*   1 teaspoon salt

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup full-fat plain yogurt
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tablespoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/2 teaspoon tandoori masala (optional, but enhances flavor)
*   1 teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
*   2 tablespoons mustard oil (or vegetable oil)
*   Red food coloring (optional, a few drops for traditional color)

For Grilling:
*   Charcoal
*   Wood chips (optional, for extra smoke)
*   Oil for brushing the grill grates

## Step-by-Step Instructions
1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Rinse the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make deep gashes (2-3 per piece) on the chicken. This helps the marinade penetrate deeply. In a large bowl, rub the chicken with lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Let it sit for 15-20 minutes.
2.  **Make the Marinade:** In a separate large bowl, combine the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, black pepper, tandoori masala (if using), the remaining 1 teaspoon of salt, mustard oil, and red food coloring (if desired). Mix everything until well combined and smooth.
3.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the lemon-salt rubbed chicken pieces to the yogurt marinade. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight (up to 24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer the marination, the better your Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled will be.
4.  **Prepare the Grill:** About 30-40 minutes before you plan to cook, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the coals for medium-high, indirect heat. If using wood chips, soak them in water for 30 minutes, then add them to the hot coals just before grilling. The ideal temperature for grilling is around 375-400°F (190-205°C). Clean and lightly oil your grill grates to prevent sticking.
5.  **Grill the Chicken:** Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the medium-high heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until you get a nice char. Then, move the chicken to the indirect heat zone, close the lid, and continue to cook for another 20-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) at the thickest part. Baste occasionally with any leftover marinade (ensure it's cooked thoroughly if re-using) or a little oil to keep it moist.
6.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring maximum tenderness.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
*   **Quality Chicken Matters:** Use fresh, good-quality chicken. Bone-in, skin-on pieces are ideal as the skin helps retain moisture and crisps up beautifully, while the bone adds flavor.
*   **Full-Fat Yogurt is Key:** Don't skimp on the fat! Full-fat yogurt not only tenderizes the chicken effectively but also creates a richer, more robust marinade that clings well to the meat.
*   **Marination Time is Crucial:** This is arguably the most important step for authentic flavor. Marinate for at least 4 hours, but overnight (12-24 hours) will yield the most flavorful and tender Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled.
*   **Score Deeply:** The gashes in the chicken are not just for show; they allow the marinade to penetrate deep into the meat, ensuring flavor in every bite.
*   **Even Charcoal Heat:** Ensure your charcoal is evenly distributed and at the right temperature before placing the chicken. Too hot, and it will burn; too cool, and it won't char properly.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and can lead to uneven cooking and steaming instead of grilling.
*   **Baste for Moisture:** While grilling, you can lightly baste the chicken with a little oil or the leftover (cooked) marinade to keep it moist and add another layer of flavor.
*   **Add Smoky Flavor:** For an even deeper smoky profile, consider adding a handful of soaked wood chips (hickory or applewood work well) to your charcoal.

## Serving Suggestions
Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is fantastic on its own, but it truly shines when served with traditional accompaniments. A dollop of fresh mint chutney or raita (yogurt dip) provides a cooling contrast to the spices. Serve it alongside fluffy basmati rice, warm naan bread, or roti for soaking up the delicious juices. A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, and onion with lemon juice) adds freshness and crunch. Don't forget a squeeze of fresh lemon juice over the chicken just before serving to brighten all the flavors.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is hard to beat, there are many ways to adapt this recipe to suit your preferences or dietary needs:
*   **Vegetarian Options:** The same marinade can be used for paneer (Indian cheese), firm tofu, mushrooms, or mixed vegetables (like bell peppers and onions) to create delicious vegetarian tandoori skewers.
*   **Other Meats:** Feel free to experiment with other meats like lamb chops, fish fillets, or even large shrimp. Adjust cooking times accordingly.
*   **Spice Level:** Easily customize the heat by increasing or decreasing the amount of red chili powder. For a milder flavor, use more Kashmiri chili powder, which provides color without excessive heat.
*   **Grilling Alternatives:** If a charcoal grill isn't an option, you can achieve a good result using an oven broiler, an outdoor gas grill, or even an air fryer, though the smoky char of Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is truly unique. For oven broiling, place chicken on a rack over a baking sheet and broil 6-8 inches from the heat, turning until cooked through and charred.
*   **Store-Bought Tandoori Masala:** If you don't have all the individual spices, a good quality store-bought tandoori masala blend can be a convenient substitute for the spice mix.

Bringing the vibrant flavors of India into your home has never been easier or more delicious. This Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled recipe promises a dish that is not only visually stunning but also bursting with authentic taste. So fire up your grill, gather your ingredients, and prepare to impress your family and friends with this incredible Indian dinner recipe. Enjoy the journey and the mouth-watering results!
